newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude called off on technicals, supply data.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude called off on technicals, supply data.

text.p: NYMEX crude was called lower Thursday morning on technical weakness after bearish oil inventory data led to a sharply lower close Wednesday.

"We had a real bearish close after the API data, and everyone is now really skeptical about whether we are going to see the gasoline demand which was expected for spring," said Al Lindseth, manager of oil and gas hedge programs for GSC Energy in Atlanta.
Crude was called five to 10 cents a barrel lower. Heating was called flat to down 0.25 cent a gallon while gasoline was called off 0.25 to 0.50 cent a gallon.

"We are opening right near 60.00 cents in gasoline, and if we can decisively break that support level, then we can take another two cents off the products," said Victor Yu, vice president at Refco Inc in New York.
On Wednesday, May gasoline ended 1.52 cents lower at 60.38 cents a gallon. May crude settled off 48 cents to $19.35 a barrel while May heating oil finished 1.37 cents lower at 53.48 cents a gallon.
The U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) has said it expects gasoline demand to reach a record 8.1 million barrels a day this summer.

But, on Wednesday, the American Petroleum Institute (API) said in its annual outlook for the summer peak driving season that U.S. gasoline supplies should be sufficient to accomodate a 2.5 percent growth rate in demand, which is the upper range of estimates.

The outlook followed API's weekly oil inventory data it released Tuesday evening which said gasoline stocks swelled 3.63 million barrels compared with a one to two million barrel decline expected by traders. Crude stocks, meanwhile, showed a larger-than-expected increase.

Still, heating oil prices could receive some support on news Sun Co Inc, a major supplier of heating oil in the region, is without any heating oil for distributors until late next week due to an early spring cold spell in the Northeast, a Sun spokesman said.
